name: crew-panel-short-viewport
description: Regression for the tutorial step 8 report: on a short browser window the Crew panel's roster and the sections below it had no way to scroll into view. Since #1765 roster rows no longer expand inline (selecting a row opens the inspector instead), so the roster itself must overflow its bounded wrapper at 1280x600 and scroll under a real wheel gesture. Proving it needs a real wheel gesture: clickSelector and expect.usable/blocked both call Element.scrollIntoView internally before acting, a DOM API no player has an equivalent for and one that is not gated by pointer-events. This file dispatches mousemove + wheel through Puppeteer's CDP input pipeline, the way a genuine gesture hit-tests, then reads the roster's own scrollTop. The read is waitForProperty rather than a bare assert because page.mouse.wheel() resolving does not mean Chrome has committed the scroll; waitForProperty polls instead of padding with a fixed delay and fails by name, reporting the last scrollTop it saw. The roster keeps the scroll while crew activity changes (#1592), and the Train action lives in the inspector's Training section, reached by clicking the roster row.

steps.description: Employees #1 and #2 are drillers (#1 is the tutorial's train-driller subject; courses grant new qualifications only (#1388), so the driller takes the rock fragmenter licence), #3 a third driller; #4 and #5 blasters. Five rows make the roster overflow its bounded wrapper without any inline-expanded row (#1765), and crew keeps changing activity while the roster is open (#1592).
The only school that teaches driving.rock_fragmenter — no role starts with it (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATIONS).

#1592 regression, part 1. Command is a harmless placeholder (command mode has no 'wheel-scroll a panel'). While the driving_center is still a construction order, shrink to 1280x600, open Crew and wheel-scroll the overflowing roster by a real gesture. Rows are not expanded (#1765). The Train button is not asserted here; it lives in the inspector once the school stands.

expect.note: No expect.usable here on purpose: it calls scrollIntoView, which would move the roster off the scrollTop 50 the wheel left and that part 2 asserts survives.

steps.description: Drive the driving_center site to completion while the Crew panel stays open and scrolled — both drillers walk to the site and work it, so their activity changes every few ticks. Before #1592 each change rebuilt the roster and snapped its scroll back to 0.

#1592 regression, part 2. The ticks of the previous step changed the crew's activity repeatedly; the roster must still sit where the wheel left it (scrollTop 50 - a refresh may not teleport it back). Nothing in this step clicks or scrolls.

expect.note: The scroll position survived the whole construction; nothing was expanded inline.

steps.description: Completes the train-driller target. Clicking the roster row selects employee #1 and opens the inspector (#1765); its Training section carries the Train button, as in tutorial-placement-cancel.
